name: Eurocaps (Elite Dangerous) font for No Man's Sky
author: 2000gmod
description:
This mod replaces the default font of NMS with the Eurocaps font. This gives it a more serious and sci-fi look, rather than the slitghtly distracting look of the default font.
This font is also used in Elite: Dangerous, an excellent space-flight simulator, which was a big inspiration for me to do this mod.

INSTALLATION:

[list=1]
[*]Drop the .pak file of your choosing (CHOOSE ONLY ONE!)* into your GAMEDATA/PCBANKS/MODS folder.
[*]Delete the DISABLEMODS.txt file.
[*]Enjoy!
[/list] 
 
 
*If you don't want to change the default title screen of NMS, choose the 'ONLY_UI' pak file. However, if you want to change it, choose the 'UI_and_titlescreen' pak file.

files.name: Eurocaps Font for NMS

name: CHEAP BROKEN SHIP INVENTORY SLOTS
summary: Lowers the cost of repairing broken inventory/technology slots on crashed ships.
author: AlaDouche
description:
This mod changes the cost to repair broken ship slots to their minimum amount of credits.  All ship inventory slots should be 1000 credits each, while technology slots should be 2000 credits each.
Early on in the game, you're able to discover crashed ships, but it's fairly pointless because you need as much money to repair the broken slots as you would to just buy a new ship.  This mod makes it worthwhile to search for crashed ships right from the get-go.

Alters GCAISPACESHIPSGLOBALS.GLOBAL, so other mods that alter it may not be compatible.

name: Better Planet Generation
summary: A huge planet generation overhaul that aims at making your hundreds of hours of exploration in the magnificent, infinite universe of No Man's Sky less repetitive and hopefully even more memorable.
author: WoodyMontana
description:
[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][i][b]                                                     [size=6]Better Planet Generation[/size][/b][/i][/size]

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1629738968-1312445652.jpeg[/img]

[size=4][b]More planets

[/b][size=3]Better Planet Generation is a total overhaul of the planetary generation in No Man's Sky.[/size] [size=3]It improves by a significant margin the procedural aspect of the universe while at the same time respecting the original work and vision from Hello Games.[/size]

[size=3]It adds thousands of new distinct environments to the universe[/size][/size]. All of them come in five different life levels and varying placement scales and layouts. These environments were made to seamlessly combine with each other in many different ways.

Better Planet Generation is designed to bring variety to the different biomes you will visit but most of all it brings a lot of variation to the universe. Outside of the countless combinations of assets and their resulting new environments, planets you visit will present themselves differently each time. Placement layouts, scale of the regions, density, variety of assets and their respective scale, ...

No planet will look exactly the same. Unless, of course, it is a very simple one. More on that below.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1631005159-472402214.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630936034-1789086190.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1610300150-1298994048.jpeg[/img]


[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=4][b]Sub Biomes[/b][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size]

Caves and underwater sub biomes have also been entirely overhauled.

Tons of new variants have been added underground and just like on the surface, additional objects can spawn to increase variety even more.

﻿[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630410276-924973523.jpeg[/img]﻿

Underwater has been completely revamped and is now generated through a triple layered dynamic framework combining assets to generate highly varied and detailed environments.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1629738939-165524032.jpeg[/img]
[b][size=4]
Unique planets

[/size][/b][size=4][size=3]On top of all the added variety, BPG also uses a flexible dynamic generation framework that can take many shapes[/size][/size] and create countless planetary variations, even when the same environments are being used multiple times.

Each planet generated has its own selection of parts based on its biome. Some liberties have been taken when designing and attributing those parts to the various biomes. Some objects have been injected to improve variety, but some restrictions have also been applied to preserve each biome's identity. Better Planet Generation also introduces countless restored, modified or repurposed assets to the game in order to increase the variety while preserving its visual style.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630936068-132859967.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630936034-754906087.jpeg[/img]

[/size][/size][/size][/size]
[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][b][size=4]Natural Generation[/size][/b][/size][/size][/size][/size]

Better Planet Generation is a vastly different experience compared to the unmodded game and even other biome mods.
Not even taking into account the small details, it is more than likely that you will never be able to encounter all the possible assets combinations this mod can generate. Let alone in the different regional layouts each dynamic template can result in.

Each biome has access to multiple procedural templates. Each producing different results in terms of layouts and objects combinations.
Their common goal is to show you a different kind of environment each time. Aesthetically and structurally.
No more "postcard" planets where most of what there is to see is right around the corner. The scale of the generation can get extremely vast compared to the vanilla game.

Planetary generation can now affect your visual enjoyment and the gameplay.
It is a video game, after all.

A world generated at its fullest possible level and highest complexity can take you some time to fully explore on foot. Meaning seeing the most notable regions (and not all of them) and scanning everything.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630052272-1155900954.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1610300150-2086924238.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630272224-118529207.jpeg[/img]
[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][b][size=4]More Variation[/size][/b][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size]

On the other hand, Better Planet Generation also allows more simple, generic yet still visually interesting planets to see :

- Planets only covered in grass and some plants, rocks or both.
- More barren worlds dominated by giant stone or crystal spires.
- Radioactive wastelands.
- Planets dotted with trees or occasional small forests.
- Volcanic wastelands.
- Toxic fields.
- Rocky swamps.
- ...

And the list goes on and on.
[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3]The occurence of these "generic" planets only relies on probabilites. None of my templates is designed to specifically produce them.
I made sure they still looked good, though.[/size][/size][/size][/size]

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630410296-1590906166.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1626079315-1486130072.jpeg[/img]

[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][b][size=4]Different Experience[/size][/b][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size]

Better Planet Generation is not for everyone. Planets can be both very detailed in every aspect or very simple.
If you expect to always see trees and a full grass coverage on your Lush planet or anywhere else, there are other mods for that.
This is not what you should expect using BPG.

Now, whether you are a new player ready to explore an infinite universe or a more weathered one that wants to be surprised by the game again, I suggest you give Better Planet Generation a try. It won't harm your game in any way.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1629923717-282604290.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630410307-2137550589.jpeg[/img]

[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][b][size=5]WARNING BEFORE INSTALLING :[/size][/b]

Installing this mod will operate changes to the terrain in every biomes.
It is also recommended to install it while in a space station / anomaly / freighter and not on a planet's surface.
Some major updates to the mod can reset the terrain or biome lists.
I'll include a warning on the download page and the sticky when it's the case.[/size][/size][/size][/size]


Recommended :
[/size][/size]
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/968]DUD's Sky - Colors[/url] : load planetary colour palettes before BPG to avoid procedural textures conflicts.
[/size][/size]

name: Fast Actions 7.1
summary: Faster clicks and key pressed actions
author: Lo2k
description:
Instead of pressing a key for almost one second, this mod provides quicker or instant inputs for :
- menu selection
- creating/dismantling technology
- transfering resources to/from ship
- entering ship
- discussing with NPC
- gathering small plants
- launching refinery processing
- recovering deployable technologies

Enjoy !

﻿- instant actions : almost no delay actions (Fractal 4.13 added an in-game option but it only works for a limited range of actions)
- fast actions : between original and instant actions

[color=#ffd966]New : v7.1 fixes precise item quantity amount selection with Instant Actions. (Fast Action is untouched)[/color]

name: Exosolar's and Babs' Beyond Base Building
summary: ★ FULLY MP compatible, this mod adds an extreme degree of freedom to the vanilla base-building options
author: Exosolar Sparky NeptuneX3 Babscoole
description:
[b][color=#f1c232][size=4]What is this Mod?[/size][/color][/b]
[size=4]There are now almost 1,000 buildable base parts in vanilla No Man's Sky! It's a dream come true!
This mod adds an extreme degree of freedom to the vanilla base-building options.
This does NOT mean the mod gives you access to all buildable parts.  You still need to learn the blueprints for each.  :)
Beyond Base Building does NOT add any new build parts to the game.

Now includes all the functionality of gBase Items, [color=#ff0000]if chosen by running the Lua script[/color]:[/size]

[list]
[*][size=4]Can multiply power, extraction, and storage rates by 2, 5, or 10. WARNING: Bases built with this mod cannot be uploaded for multiplayer when using 2x, 5x, or 10x multiplied rates.[/size][/*]
[/list]
[list]
[*][size=4]EM Generators do not need a hotspot and produce 250 power.  Not enabled by default.  Must run Lua through ANUMSS and answer question "Choose a multiplier for Storage and Rates and EMAnywhere status" to generate custom mod file to enable.[/size][/*]
[/list][size=4]

It is [b]fully compatible[/b] with multiplayer, co-op building, uploading, etc, because it [i]does not add[/i] any parts, which would cause issues in multiplayer.[/size]

[size=4][color=#f1c232][b]★ Beyond Basebuilding[/b] is fully Lua scripted, with script provided for easy updating and merging [b]★[/b][/color] and carries over all of the official updates and improvements offered by Hello Games [b]plus[/b]:[/size]

[list]
[*][size=4]Most parts can be Scaled [i][color=#fff2cc]except[/color][/i] prefab building parts, [color=#fff2cc]Exocraft Geobays, Mineral/Gas Extractors and Base Computer[/color] (Door attachment points bug out when scaled, and issues persist with scaled base computers and geobays).  There may be others not listed.  Be aware, scaling breaks snapping.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Many parts can be built in a Freighter.  [color=#fff2cc][i]Exceptions[/i][/color]  include the Base Computer, Industrial Mining parts, Vehicle Summoners and planet-based teleporter.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Many parts can be built at a Planetary Base [i][color=#fff2cc]except[/color][/i] the freighter teleporter and the Orbital Exocraft Materialiser[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]All parts can be built above and below water[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]All parts can change color and material[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]All parts, which can be deleted, can be deleted without also deleting attached objects [color=#fff2cc][i]except[/i][/color] Decals and Posters[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]No build-count limits [i][color=#fff2cc]except[/color][/i] for parts related to resources harvesting, certain terminals, beacons and message capsules (and others with limits that are hard coded into the game, as they are added or changed by Hello Games).[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Unlimited Storage Containers[color=#cccccc][size=3][i]—*This does not increase actual storage amounts: Each numbered container acts as an index to the store rather than a physical box[/i][/size][/color][/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Foundation, Pavings and Communications Station can be placed anywhere (not only on bare terrain)[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Non corvette parts buildable with corvettes[/size][/*]
[/list][size=4]
Some customization of the mod is available just by running it through AMUMSS, where you'll be prompted about enabling several feature.  Even more customization can be had by editing the top portion of the Lua before processing.  See Lua usage below for link to AMUMSS install and basic usage How to.[/size]

[color=#f1c232][b][u][size=5]Disclaimer:[/size][/u][/b][/color]
[size=3]This MOD makes changes to the placement and usage setting of vanilla parts.  If the MOD is removed, the vanilla settings will be restored and parts that "violate" a vanilla setting as well as those connected may go "poof".  Best practice is to regularly backup your saves for semi-painless recovery from the unexpected.[/size]

[center][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/images/1634/95741288-1598421367.png[/img][/center]

[size=5][b][u][color=#f1c232]Installation[/color]
[/u][/b][/size]
[b]Extract archive contents to GAMEDATA\MODS

[color=#f1c232][size=4][u]Lua usage[/u][/size][/color]
[size=4][b]✦[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2626]How to use AMUMSS at No Man's Sky Nexus - Mods and Community (nexusmods.com)[/url]✦[/b][/size][/b]

[size=4][u][b][color=#f1c232]Modified Files[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[color=#d8d8d8][size=3]METADATA\REALITY\TABLES\BASEBUILDINGOBJECTSTABLE.MBIN[/size][/color]

[i][color=#cccccc][size=3]Also check out...[/size][/color][/i]
[size=5]✦[b][color=#ffdd00][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/users/58018181?tab=user+files]Exosolar's Other Mods[/url][/color][/b]✦[/size]


[center][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/images/1634/95741288-1598421367.png[/img][/center]

[size=5][u][b][color=#f1c232]Is this Mod up-to-date?[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[size=4][i][b]Any mod files which are not hidden or demoted to the "Old Files" area can be expected to work.[/b][/i]
All uploaded files (on the Files page) are maintained with their packing date and version of the MBINCompiler used to pack it. Older mod versions, no longer compatible with the current version of No Man's Sky will be demoted to the "Old Files" subsection, but will remain available for download. There are no side-effects to using this mod.[/size]

[size=4][u][b][color=#f1c232]How to update, tweak, combine, or patch the mod with AMUMSS?[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[size=4]As this mod is now Lua scripted, you can [color=#fff2cc]easily [b]update[/b], [b]tweak[/b] or [b]merge[/b] the mod yourself[/color] (if a game update breaks this PAK of the mod, or you have other PAK or Lua mods that could conflict with this one). [color=#cccccc][size=3][i]—*Click on the spoiler below for more[/i][/size][/color][/size]
[spoiler]
[size=3][u]Notes on AMUMSS:[/u]
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/957]AMUMSS[/url] tries to update [url=https://github.com/monkeyman192/MBINCompiler/releases]MBINcompiler[/url] automatically. If it fails to convert EXML/MBIN files, its likely due to a very recent NMS version update and MBINcompiler is awaiting an update too.
If so, I highly recommend you to disable your mods and wait for MBINCompiler to be updated (it's pretty quick in general).[/size]


[size=3][u][b][color=#f1c232]Updating the mod after a game update:[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[spoiler][list]
[*] [size=3]Download [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/957]AMUMSS[/url], and extract it locally,  avoid placing the AMUMSS folder in a path with special characters or in a system folder like [color=#fff2cc][i]"C:\Program Files (x86)\(...)"[/i][/color].[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Place the mod Lua script (only the .LUA file, not the .PAK file) in the [color=#fff2cc][i]ModScript[/i][/color] folder of AMUMSS.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]AMUMSS will normally auto-detect the NMS installation folder, but you can also manually edit the path in the [color=#fff2cc][i]NMS_FOLDER.txt[/i][/color] file.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Launch [color=#fff2cc][i]BUILDMOD.bat[/i][/color] in the root of the AMUMSS folder and follow the steps, selecting the option to automatically install it in the NMS [color=#fff2cc][i]MODS[/i][/color] folder.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]A new modded PAK file will be created, using the last update of the MBIN game files duly amended by the script.[/size][/*]
[/list]
[size=3]Most of the time simply recompiling the mod using the Lua script will make it compatible again. Use the latest script to ensure you adopt any mod adjustments to accommodate the latest NMS build.[/size][size=3] There are two main causes of mods not correctly updating with this method:
1) MBINCompiler needs an update to be able to decompile the latest version of the game MBIN files.
2) Structural changes have been made to the MBIN files called by this Lua script. Whilst unlikely, this will require some script rewrite and other mods are likely affected.[/size][/spoiler]

[size=3][u][b][color=#f1c232]Tweaking the mod:[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[spoiler][size=3]Use the same process as described in [color=#fff2cc][i]Updating the mod[/i][/color].
Just modify the script as you want before recompiling it. Look at the top of my scripts, you can generally edit modifiers there, or even disable/enable some features very easily.[/size]

[size=3][color=#cccccc][i]*[url=https://notepad-plus-plus.org/]Notepad++[/url] or [url=https://code.visualstudio.com/download/]VSCode[/url] are generally recommended to read EXML and Lua files, due to large file support and automatic highlighting. The [url=https://sourceforge.net/projects/npp-compare/]Compare plugin[/url] for Notepad++, and Lua is also a must-have to highlight file differences.[/i][/color][/size][/spoiler]

[size=3][u][b][color=#f1c232]Combining mods that provide Lua scripts:[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[spoiler][size=3]You'll want to do this if multiple mods affect the same MBIN file.[/size]

[list]
[*] [size=3]Place all the scripts in the [color=#fff2cc][i]ModScript[/i][/color] folder of AMUMSS.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Launch [color=#fff2cc][i]BUILDMOD.bat[/i][/color] in the root folder of AMUMSS.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Follow the step, selecting that you want to combine all the scripts into one PAK file, and the option to automatically install it in the NMS [color=#fff2cc][i]MODS[/i][/color] folder.[/size][/*]
[/list]
[size=3]AMUMSS will output a PAK file that will contain the modifications of all the scripts.[/size]
[color=#cccccc][size=3][i]*If the scripts modify the exact same values in the MBIN file, the last loaded script will overwrite the preceding script values.[/i][/size][/color][/spoiler]

[size=3][u][b][color=#f1c232]Patch in the mod to make it compatible with other PAK files:[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[spoiler][size=3]You will want to do this if another mods isn't Lua scripted, and affects the same MBIN file as the Lua scripted mod.

It will work when :
Case 1) you patch a Lua scripted mod for only one other PAK.
Case 2) you patch a Lua scripted mod for several other PAKs, but only if the other PAKs don't modify the same MBIN files between them.[/size]

[size=3][b]How to create a patched PAK:[/b][/size]

[list]
[*] [size=3]Copy the script and the other mod(s) PAK(s) in the [color=#fff2cc][i]ModScript[/i][/color] folder of AMUMSS.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Launch [color=#fff2cc][i]BUILDMOD.bat[/i][/color] in the root folder of AMUMSS, and follow the steps, selecting the option to automatically install it in the NMS [color=#fff2cc][i]MODS[/i][/color] folder.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]The new PAK file will contain all the Lua script modifications, and a compatibility patch for the other mod(s) PAK(s).[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Rename it something like [color=#fff2cc][i]"__zzz Scripted Mod Name -Patched For- The Other Mod Name.pak"[/i][/color].[/size]
[size=3][color=#fff2cc][i]"__zzz"[/i][/color] prefix is to ensure that it'll be loaded after the mod(s) it was patched for (for NMS loading order, underscore [i]"_"[/i] came after every other characters).[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Remove the original scripted mod PAK from the [color=#fff2cc][i]MODS[/i][/color] folder, and copy both the new patched one, and the other mod(s) PAK(s), into it.[/size][/*]
[/list][size=3][u]Notes:[/u]
[b]Be sure the mod PAK you want to create a compatibility patch for, is updated for the latest NMS version.[/b]
-> When AMUSS find an MBIN file affected by a script and by a PAK in the [color=#fff2cc][i]ModScript[/i][/color] folder, it will take the MBIN file from the mod PAK over the original one of the game, and will apply to it the modifications listed in the script.
So, if the MBIN file of the mod PAK is not updated, the one in the resulting patched PAK won't be either.[/size][/spoiler]
[/spoiler]

[center][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/images/1634/95741288-1598421367.png[/img][/center]
[color=#f1c232][u][b][size=5]Philosophy[/size][/b][/u][/color]
[size=4]All the erroneous limitations in building are pretty silly, aren't they? In making this mod, I paid specific attention to making sure I did not make changes that will invalidate the bases built with it from online play. Any base made with Beyond BaseBuilding will be fully viable and visible in online play, even when other players don't have this mod! It does this by only editing placement rules while you are in the building editor and not modifying any of the actual base parts themselves.
We hope you enjoy the mod and naturally, your comments are most welcome. We can also be found on the No Man's Sky Discord or reached directly at: [color=#f1c232]Babscoole #6326 [/color]or [color=#f1c232]Exosolar#5120[/color], or if its about the Lua script: [color=#f1c232]NeptuneX3#8095[/color] [size=3][i][size=4]or [/size][/i][/size][color=#f1c232]s p a r k y#0536[/color][/size]

And, of course, thanks to all of the other modders who make mods too, as we often inspect the work of other modders to learn how things are done: [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/users/12249518]RangerDulann[/url], [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/users/1964784]WoodyMontana[/url], [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/users/42286415]jasondude[/url], [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/users/38106355?tab=user+files]Gumsk[/url], [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/users/45932167?tab=user+files]Mjjstral[/url], [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/users/41291360]moddinaccount[/url], Devilin Pixy, saa044, and others have all helped us learn to mod effectively! name: Exosolar's and Babs' Expanse
summary: Large overhaul to Diversity of Space Colors. Never see the same solar system twice!
author: Exosolar and Babscoole
description:
[u][b][size=5]What is this Mod?[/size]
[/b][/u][size=4]Expanse gives space a whole new range of expression, with 768 different combinations for space background color, star color and brightness, and nebulae color with several form of color coordinations based on complimentaries in addition to the vanilla color palettes available.

Black Edition lacks any nebulae or space clouds, leaving just cold dark space, distant stars, and a lone Sun of a random color and size.

Jasondude-Exosolar Hybrid Expanse is a hybrid of the old version of Expanse, and Jasondude's Space colors.[/size]

[b][u][size=5]Philosophy[/size][/u]
[/b][size=4]The game needs more color.[/size]

[u][b][size=5]Known Side-Effects[/size]
[/b][/u][size=4]None.[/size]

[u][size=5][b]Modified Files
[/b][/size][/u][size=4]METADATA\SIMULATION\SOLARSYSTEM\WEATHER\SKYSETTINGS\SPACESKYCOLORS.MBIN
METADATA\SIMULATION\SOLARSYSTEM\WEATHER\SKYSETTINGS\SPACERARESKYCOLORS.MBIN[/size][size=4]

[size=5]✦[b][color=#ffdd00][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/users/58018181?tab=user+files]Exosolar's Other Mods[/url][/color][/b]✦[/size][/size]

[size=5][u][b]About Available Versions
[/b][/u][/size][size=4]I keep all of my uploaded files marked (on the Files page) with their packing date and version of the MBINCompiler I used to pack it. Any older mod that is no longer compatible with the current version of No Man's Sky will be demoted to the "Old Files" subsection, but will remain available for download. If I have missed one, please tell me.

[i][b]This means that any mod files which are not hidden or demoted to the "Old Files" area can be expected to work.[/b][/i][/size]

[size=4]MBINCompiler versions exactly match the version of No Man's Sky that was current when the MBINCompiler was made, as does the MOD version number. In other words, MBINCompiler version = NMS version. This fact can be used to figure out which Legacy mods work with which Legacy versions of No Man's Sky.

[b][u][size=5]Installation[/size]

[/u][/b]Extract archive contents to GAMEDATA\MODS[/size]

[size=5][u][b]Credits and Special Thanks![/b][/u][/size]
[size=4]Hello Games for making the wonderful, vast, and fun game, No Man's Sky!
monkeyman192 for the MBINCompiler and his continued efforts to keep it up-to-date
Tub0Crisco for the No Man's Sky Mod Station A.K.A. NMSMS

[b]Big thanks[/b] to any and all of you lovely people who offer donations! It is greatly appreciated, and will help me buy lunch while I'm busy being a broke college student! :D[/size]

[size=4]And, of course, all of the other modders who make mods too! summary:
Triples the Maximum allowable tech for a total of 9. Scan times cut in half and doubled
hotspot scanning range. Torch radius to 360 degrees, with slightly brighter yellow glow.
author: Ratan Kabidge
description:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
This simply triples the allowable tech groups, to a total of 9. XanthicDragon has also
done one for a 3x3 (8 max, mod# 1229) but I find I prefer 9 as it works out better in a 8x6 
maximum size grid for my ship as shown in the image (Phase Beam is all you need with ship
targeting increases like my mod# 1318).

Update for 2.23 cut scan times in half and doubled hotspot scanning range. Torch radius 
increased to 360 degrees with increased intensity and a yellowish hue.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Files effected in this MOD are:
\GCGAMEPLAYGLOBALS.GLOBAL.MBIN
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Installation, as always:
1) Create the MODS folder within  ...No Mans Sky\GAMEDATA\PCBANKS if it does not exist.
2) Unzip and copy the "ZRatCraft - 9MaxTech 2.22.pak" file to the MODS folder.
3) Rename or delete the DISABLEMODS.TXT file if it exists.
4) Start the game and start stacking your tech.
-Rat

name: Better Rewards
summary: Increase the amount of currency you get with faster word learning and increased resource gathering options. Frigate (Freighter) Expeditions are also included!
author: MrTrack
description:
Better Rewards increases the amount of units, nanite clusters and quicksilver you get from completing missions or interacting with objects in the world. Non npc word learning (such as knowledge stones and dictionaries) is also faster.

[color=#bf9000][size=3]IMPORTANT NOTE: Don't use this mod when I haven't updated it to the new game version (especially when it is a new or returning expedition)
[/size][/color][color=#bf9000]if you really want to use it when I haven't updated it yet, make sure you [/color][color=#bf9000]back up your save[/color][color=#bf9000] or build the mod using the lua scripts yourself.[/color]

[b]Currency[/b]

Currency gain is roughly increased by 5 times, so as to make it a viable option besides crafting and selling valuable trading goods. Some unit values were tremendously increased (eg.: from minimum amount of 1000-2000 to 20000-50000) like the terminals in abandoned settlements to make the early game less grindy.

Includes:
[list]
[*]Space station missions and Nexus missions
[*]Interactable objects/devices (abandoned buildings, damaged machinery, waypoints, etc.)
[*]Sentinels
[*]Alien interactions
[/list]
[b]Words[/b]

Learning words from non npc interactions (knowledge stones and dictionaries) is also 3 times faster (3 words learned form a single knowledge stone). You now also learn 5 Atlas words, instead of 1 and also have a chance (15%) to learn them when interacting with non npc learning sources.

[b]Resources

[/b]When gathering with the mining beam you generally get 2 times more resources (but only when the things explode as you mine them). Also includes containers, depots, guild rewards, asteroids and ships that drop resources.

[b]Frigate (Freighter) Expedition Rewards

[/b]After a successful expedition, when collecting your rewards you get 5x more units and nanites, 2x more products like Storage Augmentation and NipNip Buds and 3x more resources like Copper, Emeril and Cadmium.
[b]
Installation

[/b]Make sure you delete or edit DISABLEMODS.TXT in your game library (...\Steam\steamapps\common\No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\PCBANKS) before trying to use mods. Extract the zip file to ...\Steam\steamapps\common\No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\MODS folder and you are good to go (Create MODS folder if you don't have one). Alternatively you can just use Vortex to download and install.

This mod modifies the [color=#ff0000][size=3]REWARDTABLE.MBIN[/size][/color] and [color=#ff0000][size=3]EXPEDITIONREWARDTABLE.MBIN[/size][/color] file and will not work with other mods that use those tables.

[b]Updated to NMS version 6.21 (Build ID: 21918502) on 2026.02.13.[/b]

name: Realistic Faster Movement Speed
summary: Increases movement speed, but by a realistic amount. 1.6x to walk speed and 1.5x run speed
author: Ace041
description:
[size=4][color=#3c78d8][size=5]What Does This Mod Do?
[/size][/color][/size][list]
[*]Multiplies walk speed by about 1.6
[*]Multiplies run speed by about 1.5
[/list][color=#3c78d8][size=5]Inspiration
[/size][/color][list]
[*]I didn't like the other mods that increased your base movement speed to an unrealistic amount. I wanted something that was more realistic so I used lower multipliers. This mod changes the walk speed to be more of a 'jog' and the run speed to be more of a 'sprint.'
[/list][color=#3c78d8][size=5]Compatibility
[/size][/color][list]
[*]This mod modifies GCPLAYERGLOBALS.GLOBAL.MBIN and thus will not be compatible with any other mod that modifies that file.
[/list]

name: NomNom
summary: NomNom is the most complete savegame editor for NMS but also shows you additional information around the data you're about to change. You can also easily look up each item individually to examine its attributes, independently of a savegame, or get other useful information that are not related to a specific one (but enhanced if one is loaded).
author: zencq
description:
[color=#e69138][size=3][b]NomNom is now in beta state.[/b] This means for you that some things may still not be 100% finished but the general state of the tool is a lot better than before.[/size] If you encounter bugs or when you think something doesn't work as expected or could be improved, [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1566?tab=bugs]let me know[/url]![/color]

[color=#ff0000]All available features are tested while implemented but mistakes can happen, so be aware of that and backup your saves![/color]

The features can be divided into the different main parts:
[list]
[*][b]Manager[/b] Manage your saves!
[list]
[*]Automatic backup.[/*]
[*]Save your save as human-readable JSON.[/*]
[*]Copy, move, and swap slots to another.[/*]
[*]Delete your save.[/*]
[/list][/*]
[*][b]Editor[/b] Edit your save for your needs!
[list]
[*]Ability to manage fleets, change data values like currencies and stats, and organize inventories.[/*]
[*]Ability to fast travel to any system you like, trigger space battles, and clear portal interference.[/*]
[*]Ability to edit your knowledge and recorded experiences.[/*]
[/list][/*]
[/list]
Have a look at the screenshots as well, to see what NomNom is capable of.

Each version of NomNom is built with the latest game version (at that time) in mind and the version number is reflecting that. Each one is also backwards
compatible down to [b]Beyond 2.11[/b] and even saves before that can still be edited via the build-in JSON editor. If you use it with a newer game version branch than
the one it was built for (e.g. [b]7.00[/b]), things should work as usual in most cases but there can always be a breaking change.

NomNom is compatible with every platform No Man's Sky is available on (some work better than others though). You can select a specific account/folder with you saves or, for platforms on PC, one level above if you have multiple accounts. A complete and always up-to-date overview with additional notes can be found [url=https://github.com/zencq/libNOM.io?tab=readme-ov-file#getting-started]on GitHub[/url].


[b]Instructions[/b]
[list=1]
[*]After downloading and extracting the zip file you'll find a few files. All you need to care about is the executable ([b]NomNom.exe[/b]) but new folders may    be created at runtime (e.g. for backups) that will become relevant to you.[/*]
[*]You may want to create a shortcut to the executable for easier access.[/*]
[*]As the tool includes an automatic backup functionality you don't need to do it manually but if you want to be absolutely safe, do it.[/*]
[*]At first start the tool locates your saves at the default location of each platform but if that fails, you must select it manually.[/*]
[*]Select a slot.[/*]
[*]Start tinkering![/*]
[/list]

If you like NomNom and want to support me in its further development, you can do so via the donation options above or on [url=https://www.buymeacoffee.com/cengelha]Buy Me a Coffee[/url], [url=https://github.com/sponsors/cengelha]GitHub[/url], [url=https://ko-fi.com/cengelha]Ko-fi[/url], and [url=https://www.patreon.com/cengelha]Patreon[/url]. I will appreciate it!
There won't be a paywall though.

The is also a dedicated [url=https://discord.gg/nomnom-762409407488720918]Discord[/url] server where you'll find all information in one place, firsthand. Please read the rules first, to gain full access. If you need (or want to offer) help, found a bug, have a suggestion, or something else regarding NomNom, you will find, or can post it there.

Issues created here on Nexus Mods or via another channel will of course also be addressed.


Header image by [url=https://patreon.com/Orioto]Orioto[/url]﻿.

MBINCompiler versions exactly match the version of No Man's Sky that was current when the MBINCompiler was made. In other words, MBINCompiler version = NMS version. This fact can be used to figure out which Legacy mods work with which Legacy versions of No Man's Sky.

name: Multiple player freighters on the same system in multiplayer
summary: This mod disables the restriction to warp a freighter into a system with another player freighter already present.
author: Danilotumix
description:
[b]WHAT THIS MOD DO:[/b]

Normally, when you try to warp your freighter in a system where another's player freighter is present, the game prevents it with the message "Other players freighter already present". What this mod does is remove that restriction.

It does that by modifying the file GCDEBUGOPTIONS.GLOBAL.MBIN (so it will conflict with any mod that already modifies it). The only change that this mod does on that file is changing the flag for MultiplePlayerFreightersInASystem from false to true.

It does the same as [url=https://nomansskymods.com/mods/freighter-control-allows-multiple-player-freighters-in-system/]this one[/url]﻿ but for the latest version of the game.

[b]WARNING:
[/b]
Just to be sure, make a backup of your savefile before trying this mod.

[b]NOTES:[/b]

If you have this mod and other people in your party doesn't, the other players will still be able to see and visit your freighter like normal, even if another player's freighter is already present in the system.

Only the players with this mod installed will be able to override the freighter limit in a system. Take this into account if you plan to play with people that doesn't have it. For example, if you're playing with a friend, and you have the mod and your friend doesn't, if you warp your freighter first inside a system, your friend will not be able to warp theirs. In that case, I would recommend that your friend warp their freighter first and then you, but taking into account that, after your freighter arrives at the system, your friend will not be able to move or warp again theirs.

[b]INSTALLATION:

MANUAL

[/b]Put the file MultipleFreightersMultiplayer.pak in the folder:

No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\PCBANKS\MODS

In addition to that, you have to remove or rename the file DISABLEMODS.TXT in:

No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\PCBANKS

[b]USING AMUMSS

[/b]Put the file MultipleFreightersMultiplayer.lua in your ModScript folder and run BUILDMOD.bat

NOTE: For the .lua file to work, the MBIMCompiler used by AMUMSS must support the No Man's Sky version mentioned in the filename.

name: Fast Refiners
summary: Refiners & Food Processors 10 times faster. Added an "Instant Refiners" variation for all you cheaters out there ! Compatible with NMS "THE SWARM" v.6.44 (Steam's build 23583900).
author: wim95 - NooBzPoWaH - Backing vocals by Babscoole
description:
[center][b]Description[/b] :

This Mod makes Refiners Speed 10 times Faster or Instantly !
(Personal, Portable, Medium & Large ones)
Same goes for Food Processor !


**********************************************************************************************************************

[b]Installation Instructions[/b] :

[b]Manually[/b] :

Place the "[b]Fast Refiners[/b]" [b][color=#00ffff]or[/color][/b] the "[b]Instant Refiners[/b]" folder (inside the zip file) in your
[b][color=#00ffff]InstallPath\No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\MODS folder[/color][/b].

[b][color=#ff0000]Beware NOT in No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\PCBANKS\MODS folder anymore !!![/color][/b]

or

[b]Via Vortex[/b] (Nexus new Mod Manager) :

Just click on the "[b]Mod Manager Download[/b]" button.


**********************************************************************************************************************

[b]Compatibility[/b] : 

[color=#00ffff]Compatible with [b]NMS[/b] "[url=https://www.nomanssky.com/swarm-update/]THE SWARM[/url]" v.[url=https://www.nomanssky.com/release-log/]6.44
[/url]( Steam's Build [url=https://steamdb.info/app/275850/depots/]23583900[/url] )[/color]

[b][u][color=#ff0000][size=4]3xperimental branch is not supported ![/size][/color][/u][/b]


[b]Modified File[/b] :

[color=#00ffff]METADATA\REALITY\TABLES\[b]NMS_REALITY_GCRECIPETABLE.MBIN

[/b][/color][size=2][b][color=#ff00ff]Thanks[/color][/b] to [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/users/1940575]BladehawkeX[/url] it is now provided as a patch/snippet (EXML).[/size]


**********************************************************************************************************************

[b]Merging/Updating Process[/b] :

An .lua file is provided as well to be merged via "[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/957/]AMUMSS[/url]" with any other Mod
providing some lua file(s) and modifying '[b]NMS_REALITY_GCRECIPETABLE.MBIN[/b]'.

To merge Mods with the latest release of "[url=https://github.com/HolterPhylo/AMUMSS/releases/]AMUMSS[/url]" (v5.4.1.1W+) it's real easy !

First of all install/update your [url=https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/download/dotnet].NET[/url] to (at least) the latest 6.0 Desktop :
[url=https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/download/dotnet/thank-you/runtime-desktop-6.0.36-windows-x64-installer]https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/download/dotnet/6.0[/url]
(at the time i'm writing this it's ".NET Desktop Runtime 6.0.36")
As long as you're at it install/update .NET [url=https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/download/dotnet/8.0]8.0[/url], [url=https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/download/dotnet/9.0]9.0[/url] & [url=https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/download/dotnet/10.0]10.0[/url].

You would have to choose an .lua file from the Mod you'd want to merge and the one from our Mod,
put them both in the "ModScript" "[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/957/]AMUMSS[/url]" folder, run "BUILDMOD.bat",
answer whatever you want to the questions asked,
let it do its thing and get the folder (that can be renamed to whatever)
from the "CreatedMODS" folder,
if you choose not to put it straight into your MODS folder,
then put it there and delete both of our old folders.

For more details or updated ones check out "[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2626]How to use AMUMSS[/url]".

[b]That merge needs to be done again every time a Mod is updating ![/b]

Updating the Mod (in case i'm not around to do so)
is the same process as above with only our .lua file instead of two or more.


**********************************************************************************************************************

[b]Uninstallation[/b] :

Such a sad and awful thing to do...

Delete the "[b]Fast Refiners[/b]" or "[b]Instant Refiners[/b]" folder from your
MODS folder, or Disable/Uninstall and Remove it via Vortex.

That's it. Bye Bye ! ;)


**********************************************************************************************************************

[b]Disclaimer[/b] :

Since Nexus last move (Collections and deletion policy) wim95 has lost trust/faith in Nexus,
and i for sure can't blame him for it.
As a result he took all his Mods down and gave me permission to updload a new "Fast Refiners" Mod.

[b][color=#ffd966]So Big Shout Out and Many Thanks to him for it in the name of the community ![/color][/b][/center]

Author = "alchemist"
ModName = "GPS"
BaseDescription = [[Пересмотрены возможности грузовых кораблей, судов и сигнальных сканеров.
Поиск ближайшего здания по типу или планеты по биому. Дополнительные расходы и требования к технологиям.
https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2144]]
GameVersion = "5-01-1"
ModVersion = "2-6-0"
-- =========
-- CONSTANTS
-- =========
LANGUAGE_NAMES = {"English", "French", "Italian", "German", "Spanish", "Russian", "Polish",
  "Dutch", "Portuguese", "LatinAmericanSpanish", "BrazilianPortuguese", "SimplifiedChinese",
  "TraditionalChinese", "TencentChinese", "Korean", "Japanese", "USEnglish"}
-- ========================
-- BEGIN TRANSLATOR SECTION
-- ========================
-- Hello, my name is...
TranslationAuthor = "mer1tornexus"
-- The language provided by this build. Used in the output file name and (possibly)
-- to select which file to inject language entries in to.
--
-- Select from LANGUAGE_NAMES array above.
LanguageName = "Russian"
-- When 'false', will inject language into existing files, using LanguageFilePrefix.
-- When 'true', will create seperate files for the mod in the LANGUAGE folder.
-- When 'true', adds entries to GCDEBUGOPTIONS.GLOBAL.MBIN to register the new files.
CreateSeperateLanguageFiles = true
-- Whether to create/inject the language entries into just the target language's 
-- file (false), or all language files (true). If true, players will see the 
-- provided strings no matter what language they play in. Should probably be true, 
-- unless you have a specific reason not to. Only used
-- when 'CreateSeperateLanguageFiles = false'.
ForceAllLanguageFiles = true
-- Which group of files from the "Language" directory of the extracted game files to
-- inject the new language entries into. Translators should not change. Only used
-- when 'CreateSeperateLanguageFiles = false'.
LanguageFilePrefix = "NMS_LOC7_"

# Adding Language Entries
The LANGUAGE_TABLE is a key-value table. When asked to display text, the game will
look up the the key in the player's preferred language file.
Mod Authors: Add key-value pairs. Keys must be unique across the entire game.
Translators: Make changes to the values, do NOT make changes to keys.
  ["KEY"] = "Value",
All entries should be single line strings. If the output should be a multi-line
string, use \n to denote line breaks.
  ["MULTILINE_KEY"] = "This is the first line.\nThis is the second line.",
Line-breaks are especially important in dialogs as it also indicates where to
wait for the player to hit a button to continue reading.
The link below is for a guide on NMS text formatting. This will allow you to change
the color of text or add icons. Format wrappers and icon tags must be in English.
  https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2134
IMPORTANT: Translators, be sure this file is saved in UTF-8 encoding. Any other
encoding throw errors during the AMUMSS build cycle due to a mismatch with the game
files.
--]]

-- ======================================
-- END TRANSLATOR SECTION // BEGIN AMUMSS
-- ======================================
-- this could likely be much better
local function escapeLang(value)
  value = value:gsub("<", "<")
  value = value:gsub(">", ">")
  value = value:gsub("\n", "")
  return value
end
local function langEntry(language, value)
  return [[
      <Property name="]]..language..[[" value="]]..value..[[" />
]]
end
local function TkLocalisationEntry(lang, id, value)
  local entries = ""
  for i = 1, #LANGUAGE_NAMES do
    if LANGUAGE_NAMES[i] == lang then
      entries = entries..langEntry(LANGUAGE_NAMES[i], escapeLang(value))
    else
      entries = entries..langEntry(LANGUAGE_NAMES[i], "")
    end
  end
  return [[
    <Property value="TkLocalisationEntry.xml">
      <Property name="Id" value="]]..id..[[" />
]]..entries..[[
    </Property>
]]
end
-- build xml with LANGUAGE_TABLE associated with given language
local function buildForLanguage(lang)
  local langOutput = ""
  for key, value in pairs(LANGUAGE_TABLE) do
    langOutput = langOutput..TkLocalisationEntry(lang, key, value)
  end
  return langOutput;
end
-- build pak name
local pakName = ModName.."_Lang_"..LanguageName
if Author ~= TranslationAuthor then
  pakName = ModName.."_"..TranslationAuthor
end
-- actual AMUMSS instructions
NMS_MOD_DEFINITION_CONTAINER = {
MOD_FILENAME      = Author.."_"..pakName.."_"..GameVersion.."_"..ModVersion..".pak",
MOD_DESCRIPTION   = BaseDescription,
MOD_AUTHOR        = Author,
NMS_VERSION       = GameVersion,
MODIFICATIONS = {{ ["MBIN_CHANGE_TABLE"] = {} }}
}
local Ref
if CreateSeperateLanguageFiles == true then
  NMS_MOD_DEFINITION_CONTAINER["ADD_FILES"] = {}
  Ref = NMS_MOD_DEFINITION_CONTAINER["ADD_FILES"]
  local modRef = NMS_MOD_DEFINITION_CONTAINER["MODIFICATIONS"][1]["MBIN_CHANGE_TABLE"]
  modRef[#modRef + 1] = {
    MBIN_FILE_SOURCE = "GCDEBUGOPTIONS.GLOBAL.MBIN",
    EXML_CHANGE_TABLE = {
        {
          PRECEDING_KEY_WORDS = {"LocTableList"},
          ADD_OPTION = "ADDafterSECTION",
          LINE_OFFSET = "-1",
          ADD = [[
    <Property value="NMSString0x20.xml">
      <Property name="Value" value="]]..Author.."_"..ModName..[[" />
    </Property>]]
        }
    }
  }
else
  Ref = NMS_MOD_DEFINITION_CONTAINER["MODIFICATIONS"][1]["MBIN_CHANGE_TABLE"]
end
-- for if the filename spelling of a language is different than just string.upper()
LANGUAGE_FILENAME_TABLE = {
  LatinAmericanSpanish = "LATINAMERAICANSPANISH"
}
local function langFilenameSuffix(lang)
  local langFilename
  if LANGUAGE_FILENAME_TABLE[lang] ~= nil then
    langFilename = LANGUAGE_FILENAME_TABLE[lang]
  else
    langFilename = string.upper(lang)
  end
  return langFilename
end
local function addChangeTable(lang)
  local langFilename = langFilenameSuffix(lang)
  Ref[#Ref + 1] = {
    MBIN_FILE_SOURCE = "LANGUAGE\\"..LanguageFilePrefix..langFilename..".MBIN",
    EXML_CHANGE_TABLE = {
      {
        PRECEDING_KEY_WORDS = {"Table"},
        LINE_OFFSET = 0,
        ADD = buildForLanguage(lang)
      },
    }
  }
end
local function createLanguageFile(lang)
  local langFilename = langFilenameSuffix(lang)
  Ref[#Ref + 1] = {
    FILE_DESTINATION = "LANGUAGE\\"..Author:upper().."_"..ModName:upper().."_"..langFilename..".EXML",
    FILE_CONTENT = [[<Data template="TkLocalisationTable">
  <Property name="Table">
]]..buildForLanguage(lang)..[[
  </Property>
</Data>]]
  }
end
if CreateSeperateLanguageFiles == true then
  for i = 1, #LANGUAGE_NAMES do
    createLanguageFile(LANGUAGE_NAMES[i])
  end
else
  if ForceAllLanguageFiles == true then
    for i = 1, #LANGUAGE_NAMES do
      addChangeTable(LANGUAGE_NAMES[i])
    end
  else
    addChangeTable(LanguageName)
  end
end

name: JE's Fast Harvesters and AMU
summary: Increases the capacity and rate for Oxygen Harvesters, Atmospheric Harvesters and Automated mining Units as well as allowing them to be 'picked up' for redeployment elsewhere.
author: Jaggid Edje
description:
The purpose of this mod is to make the 'returns' from the Oxygen Harvester, Automated Mining Unit (AMU) and Atmosphere Harvester good enough that a player might consider them worth having to deal with 'babysitting' them for a little while (by not leaving the system or teleporting around while they work).  With this mod, I would consider it worth setting some up before doing the derelict freighter in a system a couple of times, for example.  Without it, I would not even consider taking the time to do that.

The mod increases extraction rate and the storage capacity of Oxygen Harvesters, Atmospheric Harvesters and Automated mining Units and makes them able to be 'picked up' for redeployment elsewhere, like the portable refiner and save beacons, etc.   Mod comes in 2 versions, with capacities of either 1,250 or 2,500 (choose only ONE), both of which have a fill-up time of 30 minutes.

I also increased the fuel required for them all, by a multiple of 4x for the 1250 capacity version and 8x for the 2500 capacity version.  This still makes them slightly more fuel efficient than they were before, but not by nearly as much as they were with no fuel increase at all.   

If you prefer the lower fuel usage, feel free to compile the mod with the fuel requirement you desire.  I've made capacities, time, and fuel requirements easily changeable with variables defined at the very top of the LUA file.

[size=3]NOTICE: Any Harvesters or AMU's that are in place before the mod was installed will NOT reflect all of the changes until they are picked up and placed back down.[/size]
[size=5]WARNING: Contents of the harvesters and AMU's are not maintained or returned to the player when they are picked up.  So either empty them first, or suck up the loss.  [/size]

Modifies the following game files:
MODELS\PLANETS\BIOMES\COMMON\BUILDINGS\PARTS\BUILDABLEPARTS\TECH\GASHARVESTER\ENTITIES\GASHARVESTER.ENTITY.MBIN
MODELS\PLANETS\BIOMES\COMMON\BUILDINGS\PARTS\BUILDABLEPARTS\TECH\OXYGENHARVESTER180\ENTITIES\OXYGENHARVESTER.ENTITY.MBIN
MODELS\PLANETS\BIOMES\COMMON\BUILDINGS\PARTS\BUILDABLEPARTS\TECH\HARVESTER\ENTITIES\RESOURCEHARVESTER.ENTITY.MBIN
METADATA\REALITY\TABLES\BASEBUILDINGOBJECTSTABLE.MBIN
METADATA\REALITY\TABLES\NMS_REALITY_GCTECHNOLOGYTABLE.MBIN

LUA file included for users who want to recompile their own combined mod for compatibility.

For Game Version Cursed 5.22

No update to this mod is required for game version 5.29.

name: Vitamin Arrr's Terrain
summary: Updates the terrain generation system of No Man's Sky to make every world more of a smooth blend between extreme and normal, rather than the current game where planets are either HUGE mountains or normal, non-mountainous planets. In addition, this mod unlocks the SuperFormula to generate much more random shapes for rock & resource formations.
author: Vitamin Arrr
description:
Updates the terrain generation system of No Man's Sky to make every world more of a smooth blend between extreme and normal, rather than the current game where planets are either HUGE mountains or normal, non-mountainous planets. In addition, this mod unlocks the SuperFormula to generate much more random shapes for rock & resource formations. 

Resource formations now appear above ground and can be huge, adding epic and colorful abstract shapes to the horizon. Planet generation seeds have also been fully randomized, greatly increasing the range of possible starting seed values for the terrain generation system. 

Note: this mod is not compatible with existing base locations. I strongly recommend to use a separate playthrough save when using this mod. Future versions of this mod do not guarantee that the terrain layout will remain the same as prior versions, so you may want to version your saves along with each version of this mod.

name: Fossil and Bartering Overhaul 5.61 (RELICS)
summary: Completely overhauls Fossils and Bartering (added in RELICS) by reintroducing Rarity into the drop mechanic and making necessary adjustments to the related Bartering system.
author: Unedjis
description:
[color=#f1c232][size=5][b][color=#6aa84f][size=4][size=5]Made for RELICS (5.61)[/size][/size][/color]

Motivation[/b][/size][/color]

I love what HG did with Fossils in the RELICS update. However, I missed the randomness of the "Lootbox" system that Bone Hunting had before - finding a Purple or Gold drop just gave that little dopamine hit that caused me to spend about half of the total playtime in my current playthrough just hunting for Bones. So I decided to make a mod and reintroduce a Rarity system into the game, similar to Fishing. You will now find green C-Class, blue B-Class, purple A-Class, and golden S-Class Fossils, each with adjusted prices and drop rates.

In the same vein, the Bartering system also felt a bit flat and self-contained, allowing you to only trade Fossils for other Fossils. So I added a few other treasure-related Products as accepted items for Bartering and made a number of other adjustments to make it all work well together.


[color=#f1c232][size=5][b]Features[/b][/size][/color]

[b][color=#ffe599]Tiered Fossils[/color][/b]
[list]
[*]Fossils now come in four Tiers: [b][color=#6aa84f]C-Class[/color][/b] (50% of drops in each category), [b][color=#1e84cc]B-Class[/color][/b] (30%), [b][color=#9900ff]A-Class[/color][/b] (15%), and [b][color=#f1c232]S-Class[/color][/b] (5%).
[*]Prices have been adjusted accordingly: Skulls are the most expensive (C-Class = 150k, S-Class = 1.5M), followed by Ribcages (100k-1M), Tails (75k-750k), and finally Limbs (50k-500k). (By comparison, in Vanilla every single Fossil is worth exactly 72k.)
[*]Due to their great variety, there are many different S-Class Skulls. However, since there is only a limited number of different Ribcages/Limbs/Tails, each of those categories only has one S-Class item.
[*]Also adds five previously unobtainable Fossils to the regular drop/shop lists.
[/list]
[b][color=#ffe599]Bone Shop Bartering[/color][/b][list]
[*]Bone Shops no longer offer every single Fossil there is. Instead, each shop will offer a total of 6 to 16 different Products, including the newly-added and always present Ancient and Trident Keys (so 2 Keys + 4-14 Fossils per shop). The reasoning behind this is that with the introduction of Rarity, it should no longer be possible to just buy any particular Fossil you want. If you want to catch 'em all, you'll have to go on many Bone Hauls and/or fly to a lot of different Stations to barter for the missing pieces. The Keys have been added because the Ancient Key can be used to increase Explorer's Guild standing, and Underwater Ruins always have three chests but only one Trident Key, so by buying more of them, you'll be able to loot more treasure from under the sea.
[*]The mod also adds a variety of non-Fossil Products as acceptable Bartering currency. All of those Products are "treasure"-related, i.e. items you can find on the surface of planets, such as Storm Crystals, Gravitino Balls, Vortex Cubes etc. (For a full list, check the Documentation PDF.)
[*]To make some of those products viable for Bartering, their Bartering value has been adjusted (NOT their Unit price, except for Keys, which have had their base price increased so they're at least remotely useful for Bartering).
[*]One key piece for Bartering is the Vigilant Stone, which you can get by Disturbing the Eye at Fossil Beds and defeating the Stone Guardians. Notably, the Vigilant Stone is the single most efficient Bartering item, so selling them at a Trade Terminal is discouraged because you can actually turn a profit by using 1-3 of them to barter for A-Class or even S-Class Fossils (which are worth far more than the 102k Units you'll get if you just sell them). This is to incentivize players to actually fight the Stone Guardians and not just ignore them.
[/list]
[b][color=#ffe599]Digsite Wheelbarrows[/color][/b]
[list]
[*]The Wheelbarrows at the newly-added Digsites (NOT the ones at Harmonic Camps!) now have a chance to drop a quantity of Mineral Trade Commodities (i.e. Dirt all the way up to Re-latticed Arc Crystals).
[*]Those Minerals can now also be used for Bartering, although they're not very effective for it.
[/list]
[b][color=#ffe599]Storage Containers[/color][/b]
[list]
[*]Storing all of those different Fossils will quickly clutter up any and all of your inventories. To somewhat alleviate that, I have decided to increase the storage capacity of Storage Containers by unlocking two additional rows of slots (from 10x5 to 10x7).
[*]HOWEVER, these changes only apply to [b][color=#ff0000]new games[/color][/b]. If you want to have a bigger Container inventory on an existing save, you must first have this mod installed and then use a [b][color=#ff0000]Save Editor[/color][/b] (for example [url=https://github.com/goatfungus/NMSSaveEditor]the one by Goatfungus[/url]﻿) to unlock the two bottom rows.
[/list]
[color=#f1c232][size=5][b]Technical Stuff
[/b][/size][/color]
✅ EXML Patch Mod that edits the following files:
[list]
[*]METADATA/REALITY/DEFAULTREALITY
[*]METADATA/REALITY/TABLES/INVENTORYTABLE
[*]METADATA/REALITY/TABLES/NMS_MODULARCUSTOMISATIONPRODUCTS
[*]METADATA/REALITY/TABLES/NMS_REALITY_GCPRODUCTTABLE
[*]METADATA/REALITY/TABLES/REWARDTABLE
[/list]
Due to its EXML nature, the mod should be compatible with other EXML mods that edit the same files but not the same exact properties.

If you want to make this modular (for example you like the new Rarities but not the changes to the Bartering system), please consult the Readme/Documentation PDF, which has information on which changes are made in which file.

[color=#f1c232][size=5][b]Installation[/b][/size][/color]

1) Download ZIP file.
2) Extract ZIP file.
3) Place entire "U_FaBO 5.xx" folder in /steamapps/common/No Man's Sky/GAMEDATA/MODS folder.
4) Profit!!!


[color=#f1c232][size=5][b]Credits[/b][/size][/color]

Thank you to Gumsk and especially FriendlyFirePL, who have been very helpful in giving me a few valuable pointers and feedback.

name: Living Ship - Increased Pulse Jump Speed
summary: Increased living ship pulse jump speed to match the max possible pulse jump speed of a regular ship.
author: maryxxjane
description:
[size=4][b]Description[/b][/size]
[color=#D4D4D8]Living Ships don't have any tech equivalent to the Sub-Light Amplifier, one of the best techs imo because it saves so much time. This mod increases the Pulsing Heart jump speed just enough to match the max possible Pulse Engine jump speed of a regular ship.[/color]

[color=#D4D4D8]To clarify, with the pulsing heart in a supercharged slot, the pulse jump speed of a living ship will be the same as a regular ship with the pulse engine in a supercharged slot + the sub-light amplifier also in a SC slot with 4 pulse drive techs giving it adjacency bonuses. Check the layout img.[/color]

[size=4][b]Installation instructions[/b][/size]
[color=#D4D4D8]Put "Living Ship Pulse Speed" folder into [b][i]\Steam\steamapps\common\No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\MODS[/i][/b]. If the mods folder does not exist, create it.[/color]
